01.

The petitioner through the medium of the instant petition has sought following directions:-
02.

Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that respondent no. 2 has invited tenders for construction of the road under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, from Khandi Gali to Kanthol JK-12 PMGSY phase 4th vide NIT no. 01/PMGSY/J/01 dated 27.02.2007 Division Budhal District Rajouri.

03. He further submits that the above said road was sanctioned during the financial year 2011-12 from Khandi Gali to Kanthol but the same stands constructed by realigning from Khandi Gali to Thakuri Mal.

Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that the distance between Khandi Balwant Singh Age 62 Years vs State Of J&K on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4495427/
1 Gali to Thakuri Mal is about 5 km whereas the realigning of the said road has been done intentionally and deliberately by the contractor in connivance with the respondents to get more benefit by increasing the length of the road and the said realignment has been done without any prior notice to the inhabitants of the area.

entities.text: Khandi Balwant Singh Age 62 Years vs State Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 04. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner further submits that the said road has been constructed by the department on private land of the petitioner and that too without issuing any prior notice under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act by the Collector or initiating the proper acquisition proceeding as envisaged under law.

05. It is further submitted that inspite of the fact that the landed property of the petitioner has been used for the construction of the road, the petitioner has not been compensated so far and he submits that the law is settled in this regard that the right to the property is a Constitutional right, as envisaged under Article 300-A of the Constitution of India and in case the land of the petitioner is required, the same has to be done strictly following due procedure as envisaged under law and not otherwise.
06.

It is further submitted that even a legal notice in this regard has been sent to respondent nos. 2 & 4 for paying the compensation but till date the needful has not been done and hence the instant petition has been filed seeking a direction to the respondents to compensate the petitioner for his land, which has been acquired by the respondents forcibly inVillage Ladkuti falling under khasra No. 514, 516 measuring 5 kanals for the construction of road under Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana scheme from Khandi Gali to Kanthol.
07.

entities.text: Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana scheme
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Per contra, detailed reply has been filed on behalf of respondent nos. 1 to 3 and in addition to that fresh status report has also been filed on behalf of respondent nos. 1 to 3 dated 27.10.2021 and even the affidavit has been filed on behalf of Deputy Commisisoner, Rajouri on the asking of the Court by virtue of order dated 20.10.2021.

The affidavit so filed on behalf of Deputy Commissioner reveals that pursuant to the direction passed by this Court, the matter was taken up with the Additional Deputy Commissioner/Collector Land Acquisition Kotranka for detailed factual report in the matter and the Collector Land Acquisition, Kotranka vide communication No.
ADC/Coll/2023-24/03 dated 17.04.2023 has reported as under:-
(02KI-12MI) and 516 (01KI-05MI) total measuring 03 kanals and 17 Marlas situated in village Larkoti Tehsil Kotranka belonging to petitioner and other co-sharers
has come under the alignment of road namely Khandi Gali to Kanthole constructed by PMGSY Department and is being used for public purposes only.

II. That Notification under section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act with regard to land involved in the instant land acquisition proceedings stands issued by Collector Land Acquisition Rajouri vide No.
AC/LA/290-92 dated 11.06.2014.
III.
That further proceedings in the instant land acquisition proceedings could not be initiated for want of Funds Availability Certificate from the Indenting Department.

sentences.text: However, an amount of Rs. 29.00 Lacs stands deposited by the Indenting Department (PMGSY) as advance on 31.03.2017 with the Collector concerned.
The said amount has been deposited in Account Head 8443-Revenue Deposits by the Collector.
IV. That delay in the present acquisition proceedings has been caused for the reason that the indenting department could not submit the papers of indent.

However, Collector concerned Vide No. ADC/Coll/533 dated 21.10.2019, No. ADC/Coll/823 dated 15.02.2020 and No.
ADC/Coll/107-09 dated 02.11.2021 made requests for the indenting department for submission of papers of indent.

The copy of letter dated 21.10.2019, 15.02.2020 and 02.11.2021 are enclosed and marked as Annexure R2, R3 and R4 respectively for the perusal of the Hon'ble Court.
V.

That the indenting Department vide communication No. CEJ/PMGSY/17396-98 dated 24.11.2021 has submitted fresh papers of indent for acquisition of aforementioned land under "The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013" and consequent upon receipt of same, the Collector concerned has initiated land acquisition proceedings.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: It has further been reported by Collector Land Acquisition Kotranka that after completion of proceedings, bonafide land ownwers will be paid land compensation.
The copy of report dated 17.04.2023 of Collector Land Acquisition, Kotranka is enclosed and marked as Annexure R5 for the perusal of the Hon'ble Court.

08. While filing the aforesaid affidavit even the respondents have placed on record a communication dated 17.04.2023 addressed by the Collector Land Acquisition, Kotranka to the District Collector/Deputy Commissioner, Rajouri explaining the cause of delay in the aforesaid communication.

From the perusal of the aforesaid communication it is apparent that the land bearing khasra No. 514, 516 total measuring 03 kanals and 17 marlas situated in Village Larkoti belongs to the petitioner along with other co-sharers, which land has been involved in construction of the road namely Khandi Gali to Kanthole by PMGSY Department and the road in question is being used for public purpose only.

The affidavit and the record further reveals that notification under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act was issued by the then Collector Rajouri on 11.06.2014, however, further proceedings could not be initiated for want of the indent by the indenting department.

09. The record further reveals that no Funds Availability Certificate/Indent was submitted by the indenting department and an amount of Rs. 29.00 lacs has been sanctioned in advance by the indenting department on 31.03.2017 vide cheque bearing No. 303852 which stand deposited in the revenue deposits.

The respondents have admitted in their reply affidavit that the indenting department could not submit the papers of the indent despite repeated requests by the Collector and the acquisition proceedings were delayed in the aforesaid project for want of indent from the indenting department which led to the non-completion of the acquisition proceedings.

The affidavit further reveals that the indenting department wide communication dated 24.11.2021 has submitted fresh papers for indent for acquisition of the land in question under the new Act i.e. the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and consequent upon the receipt of the same, the Collector has initiated the land acquisition Balwant Singh Age 62 Years vs State Of J&K on 16 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4495427/
3 proceedings.
10.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Balwant Singh Age 62 Years vs State Of J&K
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents by virtue of the aforesaid affidavit have admitted that after completion of the aforesaid proceedings bonafide land owners will be paid the land compensation which includes the petitioner as well.
The copy of the report dated 17.04.2023 of the Collector Land Acquisition has also been placed on record as Annexure R5 alongwith the affidavit so filed by the concerned Deputy Commissioner.

11. Thus, in the light of the affidavit so filed by the respondent- Deputy Commissioner in pursuant to the order passed by this Court nothing remains to be adjudicated any further in the instant petition and, accordingly, the same is disposed of with the consent of learned counsel for the parties with a direction to respondent-Deputy Commissioner, Rajouri (who although was not a party respondent in the instant petition but in terms of the order passed by this Court dated 20.10.2021 has been directed to file an affidavit) to release the compensation in favour of the bonafide land owners including the petitioner within a period of two months from the date of passing of this order subject to the verification and fulfillment of all requisite codal formalities and also after drawing satisfaction with regard to the entitlement of the petitioner to receive such compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Let the needful be done within the aforesaid period.
12. The writ petition is disposed of in the manner indicated above.
